flags.headline: Amodei's call for an industry-wide AI 'pacing' slowdown triggers a broad, global AI/chip selloff
flags.detail: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay over the weekend (Sept 12) arguing the AI industry should deliberately slow the pace of frontier-model development to let safety measures catch up, warning that without it AI could within 6-12 months be capable of coordinating agent swarms that could 'take over the internet.' OpenAI's Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Microsoft's Satya Nadella publicly echoed the call. Markets read this as a signal that AI capex/monetization timelines could stretch out: in premarket trading Monday, Nvidia fell 2.13% to $213.84, AMD fell 4.77%, Intel fell 5.29%, and Qualcomm fell 4.11%; Micron (up 240%+ YTD on AI-driven memory demand) fell 5% to $926. The move is global and confirmed across markets, not a single-source report: SK Hynix -6.4% and Samsung Electronics -4.1% in South Korea, Kioxia -6.4% in Japan, SoftBank -10% in Japan, ASML -5%+ and Infineon -7%+ in Europe. Our own book's directly-exposed names are NVDA, AMD, and QCOM (named specifically in the reporting); the broader AI-infra complex in the Growth sleeve (MRVL, NXPI, CRDO, TSM, LRCX) is thematically exposed to the same narrative but we don't have tier-1-confirmed premarket prints naming those specific tickers this morning -- our own Data Drop's premarket quotes for this whole group look anomalous (see roster_integrity data_integrity note) so we are not citing them as evidence here.
flags.thesis_link: Loosely adjacent to NVDA's listed key_risk ('AI spending cycle concentration risk -- if hyperscaler AI investments fail to deliver adequate ROI, a correction in $200B+ annual data center capex would severely impact NVIDIA's revenue') and AMD's key_risk on AI infrastructure capex moderating -- but the actual trigger here is a safety-driven pacing call, not an ROI-driven capex pullback, so this is not marked as a direct thesis-risk hit, just a related mechanism worth watching if it persists.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance -- 'MU, SNDK, INTC, AMD: Chip Stocks Slide After Anthropic Calls For AI Industry Slowdown'
Bloomberg -- 'Anthropic CEO Says It's Time to Slow AI Model Advances'
Washington Post -- 'Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI industry needs to give safety measures time to catch up'

flags.headline: Hormuz/Gulf conflict escalates further: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline after drone attack, Brent tops $107
flags.detail: No new headlines in the last 24-48 hours, but the underlying conflict took a material step up over the prior weekend that this run is now confirming: drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory hit Saudi Arabia's 1,200km East-West Crude Oil Pipeline on Sept 10-11, prompting Saudi Arabia to shut the pipeline -- its main alternative route (~5M bbl/day) for moving crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu while the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively constrained by the ongoing US-Iran conflict. With that bypass route down and no ready alternative, oil broke above $100/bbl for the first time in months and closed that week up more than 8%; Brent was quoted around $107.65 as of Monday. This is a genuine widening of the supply-disruption story beyond the tanker/missile exchanges already being tracked, even though no further escalation has been reported since the weekend.
flags.thesis_link: Matches DVN key_risk: 'Oil and gas price volatility remains the dominant swing factor for earnings and free cash flow ... could reverse quickly given global supply dynamics.' The Saudi pipeline shutdown is a new, physical supply-side escalation of exactly that risk, not just a sentiment/geopolitical-headline effect.

evidence.source: CNBC -- 'Saudi Arabia shut down East-West crude oil pipeline after multiple attacks by drones from Iraq'
Al Jazeera -- 'Saudi Arabia shuts critical oil pipeline after drone attack: What it means'
CNN -- 'Saudi oil pipeline shut down after attack triggers fires'
